I took a half-day off today.
I'm moving to a different department next month.
grammar: 옮기다 → 옮겨요 (omgyeoyo) = move/transfer (something).

english: It is new work. So I am a little nervous.
grammar: 새롭다 → 새로운 (saeroun) = new, before a noun: 새로운 일 = new work.

english: A coworker helped, so I got used to it fast.
On Mondays there are so many meetings.
This project wrapped up well.
The manager praised me a lot.
grammar: 칭찬하다 (chingchanhada) = to praise; honored subject → 칭찬하셨어요.

english: There's a workshop next week.
I had new business cards made.
I got a company email address.
I want to work in this field.
I'm a little worried because I lack experience.
Still, I just need to learn hard.
grammar: -(으)면 돼요 = it's enough if / just need to: 배우면 돼요 (baeumyeon dwaeyo).

english: I like working with people.
grammar: -는 게 좋아요 = like doing: 일하는 게 (ilhaneun ge) = the working (of it).

english: I want to get promoted next year.
I'm building my career step by step.
I opened an account at the bank.
grammar: 계좌 (gyejwa) = bank account; 계좌를 만들다 = to open an account.

english: I opened a new bank account.
I want to open one more account.
grammar: Counters use native numbers: 하나 (hana) = one; 하나 더 = one more.

english: There's hardly any balance in my account.
grammar: 잔액 (janaek) = balance; 얼마 없다 = there's barely any left.

english: I made a separate salary account.
I updated my bankbook after a long time.
I waited at the bank counter.
I take a number and wait.
grammar: 번호표 (beonhopyo) = queue ticket; 뽑다 → 뽑고 = take one and...

english: I forgot my account PIN.
You have to bring your ID.
grammar: -아/어야 해요 = have to: 가져가야 해요 (gajyeogaya haeyo) = must take it.

english: I signed up for internet banking.
I check my balance on the app.
grammar: -(으)로 = by means of: 앱으로 (aebeuro) = via the app.

english: I put money into my account.
I withdrew a little cash.
The bank closes at four.
grammar: Clock hours use native numbers: 네 시 (ne si) = four o'clock.

english: I pay into a savings plan every month.
I signed up for a three-year savings plan.
grammar: -짜리 = one worth/of: 삼 년짜리 (sam nyeonjjari) = a three-year one.

english: I save 500,000 won each month.
grammar: Money uses Sino numbers: 오십만 원 (osimman won) = 500,000 won.

english: I want to build up a lump sum.
The deposit interest is too low.
The interest rate is 2 percent.
grammar: 퍼센트 (peosenteu) uses Sino numbers: 이 퍼센트 = two percent.

english: A saving habit is important.
I'm saving an emergency fund separately.
I save money little by little.
My savings plan matures next month.
When it matures, I'll have a lump sum.
grammar: -(으)면 = when: 되면 (doemyeon) = when it becomes/matures.

english: I'll travel with that money.
grammar: -(으)로 = with/using: 그 돈으로 (geu doneuro) = with that money.

english: I save diligently.
Looking at my bankbook, I feel proud.
grammar: 뿌듯하다 (ppudeuthada) = to feel proud/fulfilled (first person).

english: I set a target amount.
I got a new credit card.
I only use a debit card.
My card bill came out high this month.
grammar: 카드값 (kadeukap) = card bill; 나오다 → 나왔어요 = came out.

english: I paid in installments.
I bought it in three monthly installments.
grammar: 개월 uses Sino numbers: 삼 개월 (sam gaewol) = three months.

english: I paid all at once.
I swiped my card way too much.
grammar: 카드를 긁다 (kadeureul geukda) = to swipe/use a card; 너무 많이 긁다 = to overspend on it.

english: Next month I'll cut back on the card.
grammar: 줄이다 → 줄일 거예요 (juril geoyeyo) = will reduce it.

english: I've racked up a lot of card points.
grammar: 쌓이다 → 쌓였어요 (ssayeosseoyo) = piled up, accumulated.

english: I lost my card, so I reported it right away.
My card limit is maxed out.
grammar: 한도 (hando) = limit; 차다 → 찼어요 = got full/reached.

english: I find cards more convenient than cash.
grammar: -보다 = than: 현금보다 (hyeongeumboda) = than cash.

english: I checked my card statement.
I transferred money to a friend.
I sent it straight to the account.
A transfer fee was added.
grammar: 수수료 (susuryo) = fee/commission; 붙다 → 붙었어요 = got attached.

english: I pay the rent by bank transfer.
It goes out by auto-transfer every month.
grammar: 자동이체 (jadong-iche) = automatic transfer/direct debit.

english: I sent money to the wrong account.
grammar: 잘못된 (jalmotdoen) = wrong/mistaken (before a noun).

english: I called the bank and cancelled it.
grammar: -아/어서 = and then: 전화해서 (jeonhwahaeseo) = called, and then...

english: I deposited money into the account.
I withdrew money from the ATM.
There's a set withdrawal limit.
grammar: 출금 (chulgeum) = withdrawal; -아/어 있어요 = is (in a state).

english: A lot of money went out this month.
grammar: 나가다 → 나갔어요 (nagasseoyo) = went out/was spent.

english: I put loose change in the piggy bank.
I exchanged currency at the bank.
I changed it to dollars before the trip.
I took out a loan at the bank.
I'm still paying off my student loan.
The loan interest is such a burden.
grammar: 부담스럽다 → 부담스러워요 (budamseureowoyo) = feels burdensome (ㅂ-irr).

english: I have to pay interest every month.
grammar: 이자를 내다 (ijareul naeda) = to pay interest; -아/어야 해요 = have to.

english: I want to pay off the loan fast.
I paid off a bit of the principal this month.
Interest rates went up again.
I borrowed money from a friend.
I'll definitely pay it back next month.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 = I promise to: 갚을게요 (gapeulgeyo) = I'll pay it back.

english: I have no debt, so I feel at ease.
grammar: 빚 (bit) = debt; 빚이 없다 = to be debt-free.

english: If you take a loan, interest builds up.
grammar: -(으)면 = if: 받으면 (badeumyeon) = if you take/receive it.

english: I manage my credit score well.
I'm looking for a bank with low interest.
grammar: 낮은 (najeun) = low (before a noun): 이자가 낮은 은행.

english: I got a loan consultation.
I pay taxes every year.
The property tax bill came this month.
Income tax is more than I thought.
I'm getting ready for year-end tax settlement.
I got a small tax refund.
Tax is deducted from my salary.
grammar: 빠지다 → 빠져요 (ppajyeoyo) = to be taken out/deducted; 에서 = from.

english: I filed my taxes within the deadline.
VAT is 10 percent.
Because of taxes, take-home pay shrinks.
grammar: 줄다 → 줄어요 (jureoyo) = to decrease; 실수령액 = take-home amount.

english: Tax calculations are so complicated.
I keep a household ledger every day.
I tallied up this month's spending.
My spending is more than my income.
grammar: 수입 (suip) = income; -보다 더 = more than: 수입보다 더 많아요.

english: Living costs are high.
grammar: 생활비 (saenghwalbi) = living expenses; (돈이) 들다 = to cost.

english: I made a budget for this month.
I mustn't go over budget.
grammar: -(으)면 안 돼요 = must not: 넘으면 안 돼요 (neomeumyeon an dwaeyo).

english: I need to cut down on eating out.
grammar: 줄이다 → 줄여야 해요 (juryeoya haeyo) = have to reduce; 외식비 = dining-out cost.

english: I even save on coffee.
I often regret impulse buys.
I try to buy only what I need.
grammar: -(으)려고 해요 = intend to: 사려고 해요 (saryeogo haeyo) = plan to buy.

english: I give my kid an allowance every week.
grammar: 용돈 (yongdon) = pocket money/allowance; 매주 = every week.

english: The kids' education costs are really high.
I paid the utility bills on time.
The electricity bill is higher than last month.
I saved a lot of money this month.
I want to manage money well.
My husband and I keep the ledger together.
grammar: -(이)랑 = with: 남편이랑 (nampyeon-irang) = with my husband.

english: Saving has become a habit now.
grammar: 절약 (jeollyak) = thrift/saving; -이 되다 → 됐어요 = became.

target: 제 목표는 빚을 다 갚는 거예요.
english: My goal is to pay off all my debt.
grammar: -는 거예요 = is (to do): 갚는 거예요 (gapneun geoyeyo) = is to pay off.

english: I'm very interested in personal finance.
These days I'm investing in stocks.
I invest a little at a time in small amounts.
I'm happy my stocks went up a bit.
grammar: 오르다 → 올라서 (ollaseo) = because it rose (first-person 기뻐요).

english: I signed up for a fund too.
Investing always carries risk.
I don't make reckless investments.
grammar: 무리한 (murihan) = excessive/overreaching (before a noun).

english: I'm preparing for retirement from now.
I pay into a pension every month.
I've gotten interested in real estate too.
Housing prices have risen a lot lately.
grammar: 집값 (jipgap) = house price; 오르다 → 올랐어요 = rose.

english: I started studying personal finance.
I got advice from an expert.
I want to spend money wisely.
grammar: 현명하게 (hyeonmyeonghage) = wisely; -게 makes an adverb.

english: I want to slowly become well-off.
The exchange rate rose, so travel feels pricey.
I exchanged money at the airport.
I carry only a little cash around.
These days I pay almost everything by mobile.
I lost my wallet, so I remade my card.
grammar: 잃어버리다 → 잃어버려서 (ireobeoryeoseo) = lost it, and so...

english: The bank app is really convenient.
I've come to enjoy saving.
I spend money according to a plan.
grammar: 계획적으로 (gyehoekjeogeuro) = in a planned way, methodically.

english: I prepare retirement funds in advance.
Health matters more than money.
grammar: -보다 더 = more than: 돈보다 (donboda) = more than money.

english: I enrolled in university this semester.
grammar: 입학하다 (iphakada = to enroll) takes 에: 대학교에 입학해요 (daehakgyoe iphakaeyo).

english: Our university campus is really spacious.

target: 첫 수업이 아침 아홉 시에 시작해요.
english: The first class starts at nine in the morning.
grammar: 시 (si = o'clock) takes native numbers: 아홉 시 (ahop si = nine o'clock).

english: The professor makes their lectures really interesting.
grammar: 께서 (kkeseo) marks an honored subject and pairs with -세요: 교수님께서 하세요 (gyosunimkkeseo haseyo).

english: My sibling's lecture room is on the third floor.
grammar: 층 (cheung = floor) uses Sino numbers: 삼 층 (sam cheung = 3rd floor).

english: I major in business administration.
grammar: 전공하다 (jeongonghada = to major) takes 을/를: 경영학을 전공해요 (gyeongyeonghageul jeongonghaeyo).

english: My major is computer engineering.
grammar: 이에요/예요 = 'is': after a consonant 공학이에요 (gonghagieyo); after a vowel 친구예요 (chinguyeyo).

english: I'm taking six courses this semester.
grammar: 과목 (gwamok = course) counts with native numbers: 여섯 과목 (yeoseot gwamok = six courses).

english: My older brother finds his major classes hard.
My older sister likes the general-education classes.
I have as many as three classes today.
grammar: -이나 (-ina) means 'as many as': 세 개나 (se gaena = as many as three).

english: My older sister studies at the library until late at night.
During exam period there are no seats in the library.
I live in the dormitory.
I share my dorm room with a roommate.
grammar: 하고 (hago = with) joins people: 룸메이트하고 (rummeiteuhago = with a roommate).

english: Tuition goes up every year.
grammar: 마다 (mada = every) follows a noun: 해마다 (haemada = every year).

english: I really want to get a scholarship.
grammar: -고 싶다 = 'want to': 받고 싶어요 (batgo sipeoyo = want to receive).

english: I got a scholarship this time, so I'm really glad.
grammar: -아서/어서 links cause and result: 받아서 기뻐요 (badaseo gippeoyo = got it, so glad).

english: My sibling got a scholarship and is very happy.
grammar: 3rd-person feelings take -어해요: 기뻐해요 (gippeohaeyo = is glad), not 기뻐요.

english: The senior treats the juniors to a meal.
grammar: 한테 (hante) marks the receiver: 후배들한테 (hubaedeulhante = to the juniors).

english: The club meeting is on Friday evening.
grammar: 에 (e) marks a time: 저녁에 (jeonyeoge = in the evening).

english: I joined the photography club.
grammar: 가입하다 (gaipada = to join) takes 에: 동아리에 가입해요 (dongarie gaipaeyo).

english: The university festival opens next week.
A famous singer comes for the festival.
I'm going to Japan as an exchange student.
grammar: (으)로 marks a role: 교환 학생으로 (gyohwan haksaengeuro = as an exchange student).

english: Next year I'm going to study abroad in the US.
grammar: 유학을 가다 = 'to go study abroad': 유학을 가요 (yuhageul gayo).

english: Preparing for study abroad is really tough.
I prepare the visa documents in advance.
I need a foreign-language test score.
grammar: 필요하다 (piryohada = to need) takes 이/가: 점수가 필요해요 (jeomsuga piryohaeyo).

target: 저는 영어 실력을 더 키우고 싶어요.
english: I want to build up my English skills more.
I went on a language program for six months.
grammar: 개월 (gaewol = months) uses Sino numbers: 육 개월 (yuk gaewol = six months).

english: I made a lot of friends locally.
grammar: 사귀다 → 사귀었어요 (sagwieosseoyo = made friends), keeping 귀 before -었어요.

english: At first the classes were really hard.
Now I've gotten used to local life a lot.
grammar: -아/어지다 = 'become': 익숙해졌어요 (iksukhaejyeosseoyo = got used to).

english: My homestay family is really kind.
grammar: For elders, use honorific -세요: 친절하세요 (chinjeolhaseyo = is kind).

english: I come back to Korea during vacation.
Sometimes studying abroad feels lonely.
Learning new culture is really enjoyable.
My roommate is curious about my hometown.
grammar: 3rd-person curiosity takes -어해요: 궁금해해요 (gunggeumhaehaeyo = is curious).

target: 저는 여름 방학에 배낭여행을 갈 거예요.
english: I'll go backpacking this summer vacation.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 = 'will': 갈 거예요 (gal geoyeyo = will go).

english: High schoolers prepare hard for the entrance exam.
The college entrance exam is in November.
grammar: Months use Sino numbers: 십일월 (sibirwol = November).

english: My older sister takes the entrance exam this year.
The exam hall is really quiet.
On exam day the whole country is tense.
My parents pray in front of the exam hall.
grammar: 께서 + -세요 mark honored parents as subject: 부모님께서 하세요 (bumonimkkeseo haseyo).

english: Colleges are decided by the exam score.
grammar: (으)로 marks the means: 점수로 (jeomsuro = by the score).

english: My sibling found the language section the hardest.
I couldn't solve a single math problem.
grammar: 하나도 + 못 = 'not a single one': 하나도 못 풀었어요 (hanado mot pureosseoyo).

english: After the exam I felt really relieved.
grammar: -고 = 'and then': 끝나고 (kkeunnago = it ends, and then).

english: There are many students who retake the year.
My sibling is stressed because of the exam.
grammar: 때문에 (ttaemune = because of) follows a noun: 수능 때문에 (suneung ttaemune).

english: My kid goes to the academy after school.

target: 형은 영어 학원에 삼 년 동안 다녔어요.
english: My older brother attended an English academy for three years.
grammar: 년 (nyeon = years) uses Sino numbers: 삼 년 (sam nyeon = three years).

target: 학원 수업이 밤 열 시에 끝나요.
english: The academy class ends at ten at night.
grammar: 시 uses native numbers: 열 시 (yeol si = ten o'clock).

target: 수학 학원 선생님께서 정말 잘 가르치세요.
english: The math academy teacher teaches really well.
grammar: honorific -세요 for the teacher: 가르치세요 (gareuchiseyo = teaches).

english: I send my child to piano academy.
grammar: 에 marks the destination: 학원에 보내요 (hagwone bonaeyo = send to the academy).

english: The academy fees are pricier than I thought.
grammar: 보다 (boda = than) marks comparison: 생각보다 (saenggakboda = than I thought).

target: 아들이 학원에서 단어 시험을 매일 봐요.
english: My son takes a vocab test at the academy every day.
My daughter takes online academy lectures.
Internet lectures are more convenient than the academy.
My son finds the academy homework hard.
grammar: 3rd-person feelings take -어해요: 힘들어해요 (himdeureohaeyo = finds it hard).

english: My sibling has midterms next week.
Finals are already coming up.
My older brother studied all night for the exam.
The range of this exam is too broad.

target: 동생이 이번 시험을 아주 잘 봤어요.
english: My sibling did really well on this exam.
grammar: 시험을 보다 = 'to take a test': 시험을 봤어요 (siheomeul bwasseoyo = took the test).

english: My grades went up from last semester.
grammar: 오르다 is 르-irregular: 올랐어요 (ollasseoyo = went up).

english: I showed my report card to my parents.
grammar: 께 (kke) is the honorific 'to': 부모님께 (bumonimkke = to my parents).

english: My sibling failed the exam and is upset.
I studied hard and passed the exam.
grammar: 시험에 붙다 = 'to pass a test': 붙었어요 (buteosseoyo = passed).

english: This time I'll definitely pass, I promise.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 makes a promise: 합격할게요 (hapgyeokhalgeyo = I'll pass).

english: I'll prepare harder for the next exam, I promise.
The teacher announced the exam results.
grammar: honorific past -셨어요: 발표하셨어요 (balpyohasyeosseoyo = announced).

english: I'm preparing for a certification exam.
I applied for the Korean proficiency test.
grammar: 신청하다 (sincheonghada = to apply) takes 을/를: 시험을 신청해요 (siheomeul sincheonghaeyo).

english: My older sister missed the exam application period.
I want to raise my grades more.
I prepare the presentation together with my teammates.
I submitted the assignment by email.
grammar: (으)로 marks the means: 이메일로 (imeillo = by email).

english: The report is due tomorrow.
grammar: 까지 (kkaji = until) marks a limit: 내일까지 (naeilkkaji = until tomorrow).

english: I pulled an all-nighter and finished the report.
The professor gives a lot of assignments.
grammar: honorific -세요 for the professor: 내세요 (naeseyo = gives out).

english: My older sister looks for presentation materials in the library.
I was so nervous when presenting.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 때 = 'when': 발표할 때 (balpyohal ttae = when presenting).

english: I review together with my younger sibling.

target: 동생은 수업 전에 미리 예습을 해요.
english: My sibling previews before class.
I write hard words in my notebook.

target: 매일 새 단어를 열 개씩 외워요.
english: I memorize ten new words each day.
grammar: -씩 (-ssik) means 'each/apiece': 열 개씩 (yeol gaessik = ten each).

english: With the exam coming up I feel very nervous.
My sibling got touchy because of the exam.
The exams are all over, so I feel at ease.
My older brother's Korean grade is the best.
My sibling's math score dropped from last time.
The teacher explains the answers in detail.
grammar: honorific -세요: 설명하세요 (seolmyeonghaseyo = explains).

english: For problems I don't know, I ask the teacher.
grammar: 께 marks the honored receiver: 선생님께 (seonsaengnimkke = to the teacher).

english: I did well on the test so I feel good.
I hate group assignments the most.
My parents worry about my exam results.

target: 저는 방학 동안 인터넷 강의를 들을 거예요.
english: I'll take internet lectures over the vacation.
I met an elementary-school classmate after a long time.
In middle school I was class president.

target: 고등학교 삼 학년 때 진로를 정했어요.
english: I decided my career path in the third year of high school.
grammar: 학년 (hangnyeon = grade) uses Sino numbers: 삼 학년 (sam hangnyeon = 3rd grade).

english: My homeroom teacher was really nice.
grammar: honorific past -(으)셨어요: 좋으셨어요 (joeusyeosseoyo = was nice/good).

english: The students chatter in the classroom.
During break I go to the snack shop.
The school lunch was really tasty today.
My sibling gets along well with classmates.
My sibling dozed off in class and got scolded.
The teacher checks the homework carefully.
I commute to school by bus.
grammar: (으)로 marks the means: 버스로 (beoseuro = by bus).

english: During exams I'm short on sleep.
I set my goal for this semester.
Grades come out as much as you put in.
grammar: 만큼 (mankeum = as much as) follows a word: 노력한 만큼 (noryeokan mankeum = as much as you try).

english: When I grow up I want to become a teacher.
My sibling wants to become a scientist when they grow up.
grammar: 3rd-person wishes take -고 싶어해요: 되고 싶어해요 (doego sipeohaeyo = wants to become).

english: My parents cheer on my studies.
I'm really looking forward to the new semester.

target: 방학 숙제를 아직 다 못 했어요.
english: I still haven't finished all my vacation homework.
grammar: 못 + verb = 'cannot / didn't manage': 못 했어요 (mot haesseoyo = couldn't do).

english: The start of term is already next week.
My sibling makes the school newspaper.
The teacher helps with going on to higher school.
I transferred schools twice.
grammar: 번 (beon = times) uses native numbers: 두 번 (du beon = twice).

english: I attended an international school.

target: 좋은 대학에 가고 싶어서 정말 열심히 공부해요.
english: Because I want to get into a good university, I study really hard.
My father watches the news every morning.
grammar: 마다 (mada = every) follows a noun: 아침마다 (achimmada = every morning).

english: The news these days is so depressing.
I heard the news of that accident on the news.
My grandfather reads newspaper articles every day.
The reporter reports the incident in detail.
The news anchor speaks clearly.

target: 여행 전에 날씨 예보를 보고 우산을 챙겼어요.
english: Before the trip I checked the forecast and packed an umbrella.
grammar: -고 chains actions in order: 보고 챙겼어요 (bogo chaenggyeosseoyo = looked, then packed).

english: I'm very interested in economic news.
grammar: 관심이 많다 = 'be very interested': 관심이 많아요 (gwansimi manayo).

english: Political news is too complicated.
Breaking news suddenly popped up on the screen.
grammar: 뜨다 → 떴어요 (tteosseoyo = popped up); the ㅡ drops before -었어요.

english: I read overseas news on an app.
grammar: (으)로 marks the tool: 앱으로 (aebeuro = on an app).

english: There's a lot of fake news these days.
Online papers are faster than paper ones.
grammar: 보다 marks 'than': 종이 신문보다 (jongi sinmunboda = than paper papers).

english: I only read articles I'm interested in.
grammar: 만 (man = only) follows the noun: 기사만 (gisaman = only articles).

english: When I read news comments I get angry.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when/if': 읽으면 (ilgeumyeon = when you read).

english: My sibling is on social media all day long.
My friend posted a new photo.
grammar: 올리다 → 올렸어요 (ollyeosseoyo = posted); 리 becomes 려 before -었어요.

english: I liked that post.
grammar: 누르다 → 눌렀어요 (nulleosseoyo = pressed): a 르-irregular.

english: People leave comments on my photos.
I have over a hundred followers.
grammar: 넘다 (neomda = to exceed) takes 이/가: 백 명이 넘어요 (baengmyeongi neomeoyo = over 100).

english: Popular posts have high view counts.
I often post photos of good restaurants.
I follow a famous influencer.

target: 저는 개인 정보를 온라인에 안 올려요.
english: I don't post personal info online.
grammar: 안 + verb = negation: 안 올려요 (an ollyeoyo = don't post).

english: I keep up with overseas friends' news through social media.

target: 저는 하루에 사진을 다섯 장 올려요.
english: I post five photos a day.
grammar: 장 (jang) counts flat things with native numbers: 다섯 장 (daseot jang = five sheets).

english: My sibling taps a heart on my photo.

target: 저는 SNS 계정이 두 개 있어요.
english: I have two social-media accounts.
grammar: 개 (gae) counts things with native numbers: 두 개 (du gae = two).

english: I changed my profile picture to a new one.
I switched my account to private.
grammar: (으)로 marks a change-into: 비공개로 (bigonggaero = into private).

english: A stranger sent a friend request.
I blocked that person right away.
grammar: 차단하다 (chadanhada = to block) takes 을/를: 사람을 차단해요 (sarameul chadanhaeyo).

english: There are really many people in the group chat.
We chat every day in the family group chat.
My grandmother leaves comments on my photos.
grammar: honorific -세요: 다세요 (daseyo = leaves/attaches).

english: My kid watches YouTube every night.
This YouTuber has a lot of subscribers.
I subscribed to that channel right away.
grammar: 구독하다 (gudokada = to subscribe) takes 을/를: 채널을 구독해요 (chaeneol-eul gudokaeyo).

english: When a new video is uploaded, a notification comes.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when': 올라오면 (ollaomyeon = when it's uploaded).

english: My mother enjoys watching cooking videos.

target: 영상이 너무 길어서 두 배로 봐요.
english: The video is too long so I watch at double speed.
grammar: (으)로 marks the manner: 두 배로 (du baero = at double speed).

english: I binge-watched a drama on Netflix over the weekend.

target: 가족하고 주말에 영화를 세 편 봤어요.
english: I watched three movies with my family over the weekend.
grammar: 편 (pyeon) counts films with native numbers: 세 편 (se pyeon = three films).

english: This drama has five seasons.
grammar: 개 (gae) counts things with native numbers: 다섯 개 (daseot gae = five).

english: I'm really curious about the next episode.
My friend told me the drama's ending early.
My grandmother watches dramas with subtitles on.
This movie's picture quality is really good.
I download videos and watch them.
When ads come on I get really annoyed.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when': 나오면 (naomyeon = when it comes out).

english: I look up videos of the singer I like.
grammar: 의 (ui) shows possession: 가수의 영상 (gasu-ui yeongsang = the singer's video).

target: 이 채널은 매주 새 영상을 올려요.
english: This channel posts new videos every week.
I study English on YouTube.
grammar: (으)로 marks the tool: 유튜브로 (yutyubeuro = via YouTube).

english: When I watch travel vlogs I want to leave.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when': 보면 (bomyeon = when I watch).

english: I eat while watching mukbang.
grammar: -(으)면서 = 'while': 보면서 (bomyeonseo = while watching).

english: My sibling waits for the new webtoon every week.
This webtoon's art is really pretty.

target: 웹툰 한 편을 순식간에 다 봤어요.
english: I finished one webtoon episode in an instant.

target: 유료 웹툰은 미리 볼 수 있어요.
english: With paid webtoons, you can read ahead.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = 'can': 볼 수 있어요 (bol su isseoyo = can view).

english: My kid reads webtoons on a smartphone.
That webtoon was made into a drama.
grammar: (으)로 marks the result: 드라마로 (deuramaro = into a drama).

english: I was curious about the next episode, so I paid.
Popular webtoons have thousands of comments.
I want to become a webtoon artist.

target: 웹툰을 보면 시간이 정말 빨리 가요.
english: When I read webtoons, time really flies.
My mother does all her shopping on apps.
I ordered chicken on a delivery app.

target: 이 여행 앱은 정말 편하고 빨라요.
english: This travel app is really convenient and fast.
I installed a new app on my phone.
I updated the app to the latest version.

target: 해외에서 비밀번호를 잊어버려서 로그인을 못 했어요.
english: Abroad I forgot my password and couldn't log in.
I signed up for a travel app.
I find my way with a map app.
I booked a hotel with a travel app.

target: 번역 앱이 여행할 때 정말 유용해요.
english: A translation app is really useful when traveling.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 때 = 'when': 여행할 때 (yeohaenghal ttae = when traveling).

english: I handle banking on an app.

target: 앱으로 택시를 부르면 정말 빨리 와요.
english: When you call a taxi with an app it comes really fast.
grammar: -(으)면 = 'when': 부르면 (bureumyeon = when you call).

english: I manage money with a budgeting app.

target: 운동 앱이 걸음 수를 세어 줘요.
english: A fitness app counts my steps.
I set my alarm for six o'clock.
grammar: 시 uses native numbers: 여섯 시 (yeoseot si = six o'clock).

english: I turned off all app notifications.
I save family photos to the cloud.

target: 여행 사진이 많아서 저장 공간이 부족해요.
english: I have so many travel photos that storage space is low.
I deleted all the old apps.
I back up family photos often.

target: 호텔 인터넷이 느려서 영상이 자꾸 멈춰요.
english: The hotel internet is slow so the video keeps stopping.
At the airport the wifi won't connect, so it's frustrating.
Abroad my data runs low, so I only use wifi.
My phone battery is already dead.
grammar: 다 되다 = 'be all used up': 다 됐어요 (da dwaesseoyo = is dead/empty).

english: I left my charger at the hotel.
grammar: -고 오다 = 'do and come': 두고 왔어요 (dugo wasseoyo = left it and came).

english: I lost my wireless earbuds during the trip.
I do video meetings on an app.
I use apps a lot while working from home.
grammar: -(으)면서 = 'while': 하면서 (hamyeonseo = while doing).

english: I take lectures online from abroad.

target: 저는 이메일을 하루에 스무 번 확인해요.
english: I check email twenty times a day.
grammar: 번 (beon = times) uses native numbers: 스무 번 (seumu beon = twenty times).

english: I accidentally deleted an important file.
grammar: (으)로 marks the cause here: 실수로 (silsuro = by mistake).

english: The app suddenly froze so I restarted it.
I don't answer unknown numbers.
I get way too many spam texts.

target: 저는 필요 없는 알림을 다 껐어요.
english: I turned off all the notifications I don't need.
I switched to a new phone and I'm really satisfied.

target: 아들이 게임 앱에 돈을 너무 많이 써요.
english: My son spends way too much money on game apps.

target: 아이가 게임을 너무 오래 해서 걱정돼요.
english: My kid plays games too long, so I'm worried.

target: 저는 아이의 스마트폰 사용 시간을 정해요.
english: I set my child's screen time.
My parents find using new apps difficult.
grammar: honorific of a 3rd-person feeling: 어려워하세요 (eoryeowohaseyo = find it hard).

english: I book train tickets on an app.
I got lost so I opened the map app.
Even abroad I watch Korean broadcasts on apps.
grammar: -도 (-do = even/also): 해외에서도 (haeoeseodo = even abroad).

english: I organize travel photos with an app.
Thanks to the interpreter app, the conversation was easy.
grammar: 덕분에 (deokbune = thanks to) follows a noun: 앱 덕분에 (aep deokbune = thanks to the app).

target: 저는 새 소식을 앱 알림으로 받아요.
english: I get new updates through app notifications.

target: 여행 앱에서 쿠폰을 받아서 싸게 샀어요.
english: I got a coupon on the travel app and bought it cheaply.

target: 저는 그 앱에 별점 오 점을 줬어요.
english: I gave that app five stars.
grammar: 점 (jeom = points) uses Sino numbers: 오 점 (o jeom = five points).

target: 여행 앱 후기를 꼼꼼히 읽고 골랐어요.
english: I read the travel app reviews carefully and chose.
My older sister listens to songs on a music app.
This app is free, so it's really nice.
grammar: 이다 connective -라서 = 'because it is': 무료라서 (muryoraseo = because it's free).

target: 여행 중에 매일 앱으로 일기를 써요.
english: During my trip I write a diary on an app every day.

target: 동생은 사진 앱으로 얼굴을 예쁘게 꾸며요.
english: My younger sibling makes their face look pretty with a photo app.

target: 어머니 병원 예약을 앱으로 잡아 드려요.
english: I book my mother's doctor appointment on an app for her.

target: 새로 나온 앱이 요즘 정말 인기예요.
english: A newly released app is really popular these days.
I screenshotted a photo of my kid and sent it to the family.
This app has no ads, so it's good.

target: 저는 앱 알림 소리를 진동으로 바꿨어요.
english: I changed the app alert sound to vibrate.

target: 화면이 자꾸 멈춰서 앱을 다시 깔았어요.
english: The screen kept freezing so I reinstalled the app.

target: 저는 하루에 휴대폰을 백 번 넘게 봐요.
english: I look at my phone over a hundred times a day.
We've been friends for ten years.
grammar: 된 (doen) before a time word = of that length: 십 년 된 = of ten years.

english: I don't have many close friends.
grammar: 많지 않아요 (manchi anayo) = 'not many' — long negation with 안 is also fine: 안 많아요.

target: 진짜 친구는 어려울 때 옆에 있어요.
english: A true friend is there in hard times.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 때 (-l ttae) = 'when': 어려울 때 = when it's hard.

target: 제일 친한 친구가 다음 달에 이사를 가요.
english: My best friend is moving away next month.
I quarreled with a friend over something trivial.
grammar: -(으)로 (-ro) here = 'over/because of': 일로 = over a matter.

english: I met an old friend after a long time.
grammar: 오랜만에 (oraenmane) = after a long time — a fixed set phrase.

target: 그 친구는 항상 제 이야기를 잘 들어요.
english: That friend always listens to me well.

target: 친구가 힘들어할 때 옆에서 위로해 줬어요.
english: I comforted my friend when they were struggling.
grammar: 3rd-person feelings take -어하다: 친구가 힘들어해요 (himdeureohaeyo), not 힘들어요.

english: Friendship needs effort too.
grammar: -도 (-do) = 'too/even': 우정도 = friendship too.

target: 저는 새 친구를 쉽게 못 사귀어요.
english: I don't make new friends easily.
grammar: 못 (mot) before a verb = 'can't': 못 사귀어요 = can't befriend.

target: 새 회사에서 좋은 동료를 친구로 사귀었어요.
english: I made a good colleague into a friend at my new company.
We got close quickly because our hobbies are similar.
grammar: -아/어서 (-aseo/-eoseo) = 'so/because': 비슷해서 = because they're similar.

target: 저는 친구의 비밀을 끝까지 지켜 줬어요.
english: I kept my friend's secret to the end.
grammar: -아/어 주다 (-a/eo juda) = do a favor for someone: 지켜 줬어요 = kept (it) for them.

english: He really takes good care of his friends.
We tell each other everything.
grammar: 뭐든지 (mwodeunji) = 'anything/everything' — 뭐 + 든지.

english: I chatted with a friend all night.
grammar: 수다를 떨다 (suda-reul tteolda) = to chatter — a fixed expression.

english: I really trust that friend.

target: 저는 멀리 사는 친구가 많이 그리워요.
english: I really miss my friend who lives far away.
My friend remembered my birthday.
Manners matter even between friends.
grammar: -에도 (-edo) = 'even in/at': 사이에도 = even between (them).

target: 제 친구는 제 좋은 성적을 부러워해요.
english: My friend envies my good grades.
grammar: Others envying = 부러워해요 (bureowohaeyo); for yourself say 부러워요.

target: 그 친구랑은 말이 정말 잘 통해요.
english: I click really well with that friend.
grammar: 말이 통하다 (mari tonghada) = to click / communicate well.

english: I was hurt when my friend suddenly cut off contact.
Childhood friends are the most comfortable.
grammar: 제일 (jeil) = 'the most' — same as 가장.

english: I'm so glad I met a good friend.
grammar: 다행이에요 (dahaengieyo) = 'what a relief / I'm glad' — a set phrase.

target: 두 사람이 요즘 사귀는 것 같아요.
english: Those two seem to be dating these days.
grammar: -는 것 같아요 (-neun geot gatayo) = 'it seems that': a soft guess.

english: I fell for that person at first sight.
grammar: 첫눈에 반하다 (cheonnune banhada) = to fall in love at first sight.

english: We started dating last month.
grammar: -기 시작하다 (-gi sijakhada) = 'start doing': 사귀기 시작했어요.

english: He likes her a lot.
grammar: 좋아하다 (joahada) is a verb, so 3rd person is fine: 좋아해요.

english: I was so nervous on the first date.
grammar: 긴장되다 (ginjangdoeda) = to get nervous — past: 긴장됐어요.

english: My boyfriend gave me flowers.
I talk on the phone with my girlfriend every night.
grammar: 통화하다 (tonghwahada) = to talk on the phone (vs 전화하다 = to call).

english: It's our 100-day anniversary next week.
grammar: 백일 (baegil) = the 100-day mark couples celebrate.

english: I keep thinking about that person.
grammar: 생각이 나다 (saenggagi nada) = 'come to mind'; 자꾸 = repeatedly.

english: I haven't confessed my feelings yet.
grammar: -지 못하다 (-ji mothada) = long form of 'can't': 고백하지 못했어요.

english: A friend took me to a blind date.
grammar: 소개팅 (sogaeting) = a set-up blind date.

target: 두 사람은 성격이 아주 잘 맞아요.
english: The two are very well-matched in personality.
grammar: 성격이 맞다 (seonggyeogi matda) = personalities match.

english: He really cherishes his girlfriend.
We often fight over little things.
I think you get comfortable after dating a long time.
grammar: -(으)면 (-myeon) = 'if/when': 사귀면 = if you date.

english: She misses her boyfriend a lot.
grammar: She (3rd person) misses = 그리워해요, not 그리워요.

english: Work matters more to me than dating.
grammar: -보다 (-boda) = 'than': 연애보다 = than dating.

english: We walked in the park holding hands.
grammar: -고 (-go) links actions: 잡고 걸었어요 = held (hands) and walked.

target: 그 사람이 저한테 관심이 있는 것 같아요.
english: That person seems interested in me.
I struggled a lot for a while after we broke up.

target: 저는 다시 좋은 사람을 만나고 싶어요.
english: I want to meet a good person again.
My boyfriend walked me home.
We take photos together on every anniversary.
He still doesn't have the courage to confess.
One-sided love seems really lonely.
I clash with my father often these days.
My sibling took my clothes without asking.
My parents oppose my career path.
grammar: Elders as subject take -세요: 부모님은 반대하세요 (bandaehaseyo).

english: I argued with my older brother over something trivial.

target: 어머니께서 제 성적 때문에 화가 나셨어요.
english: My mother got angry about my grades.
grammar: 께서 (kkeseo) is the honorific subject marker; verb adds -시-: 나셨어요.

english: I think very differently from my parents.
My older sister nags me a lot.
My sibling always gets angry only at me.
My father doesn't like my friends.
grammar: Honorific negation: 좋아하지 않으세요 (joahaji aneuseyo).

english: Misunderstandings sometimes arise even among family.
It's hard for me to speak honestly to my parents.
grammar: 께 (kke) = honorific 'to': 부모님께 = to (my) parents.

target: 형은 제 이야기를 잘 안 들어요.
english: My older brother doesn't really listen to me.
Whenever the holidays come, the family often quarrels.
My parents worry when I come home late.
grammar: Elders subject → 걱정하세요 (geokjeonghaseyo), not 걱정해요.

target: 동생과 방을 같이 써서 좀 불편해요.
english: It's a bit uncomfortable sharing a room with my sibling.

target: 저는 가끔 그냥 집을 나가고 싶어요.
english: Sometimes I just want to leave home.

target: 아버지는 제 결정을 잘 이해하지 못하세요.
english: My father doesn't quite understand my decision.
grammar: Honorific can't: 이해하지 못하세요 (ihaehaji mothaseyo).

target: 우리 가족은 대화가 좀 부족한 것 같아요.
english: I think our family lacks communication a bit.
grammar: -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 hedges a judgment: 부족한 것 같아요.

english: My mother and I have very different tastes.
My older brother always takes our parents' side.

target: 저는 화가 나도 최대한 참으려고 해요.
english: Even when I'm angry, I try my best to hold it in.
I was disappointed my sibling broke a promise again.
grammar: 약속을 어기다 (yaksogeul eogida) = to break a promise.

english: My parents' expectations sometimes feel a bit burdensome.

target: 가족한테 상처 주는 말을 하고 후회했어요.
english: I regretted saying hurtful words to my family.

target: 서로 목소리를 높이면 대화가 안 돼요.
english: If we raise our voices, we can't talk.
Yesterday I finally made up with my sibling.
This time I'll apologize first.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 (-lgeyo) = a promise/commitment: 사과할게요 = I'll apologize.

english: I won't say things like that again.
grammar: 다시는 ... -지 않을게요 = 'I promise not to ... again'.

english: We finally cleared up a long misunderstanding.
I told my father I was sorry.
grammar: 말씀드리다 (malsseumdeurida) = humbly 'tell' an elder.

english: My older brother reached out to me first.
If you apologize sincerely, feelings ease.
I get along with my friend like before again.
Let's stop fighting and make up now.
My mother understood my feelings.
grammar: -아/어 주시다 = do a favor (honored): 이해해 주셨어요.

english: As time passed, the hurt disappeared.
It was all my fault, I'm really sorry.
I'll do better from now on.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 promises effort: 잘할게요 = I'll do well.

english: We hugged and apologized to each other.
After making up, I felt much more at ease.
A long conflict with my brother finally resolved.

target: 제가 오늘 저녁에 친구에게 먼저 연락할게요.
english: I'll be the one to contact my friend this evening.

target: 부모님이 제 사과를 흔쾌히 받아 주셨어요.
english: My parents readily accepted my apology.
Talking honestly cleared up the misunderstanding.

target: 우리는 얼마 뒤에 다시 사이가 좋아졌어요.
english: We got along well again a while later.
We decided to each give in a little.
I promise I'll never get angry from next time.
My sibling apologized sincerely, in tears.
Our sincerity got through and we made up.
I feel so relieved now the misunderstanding is cleared.
My cousin gets married next month.
I received my friend's wedding invitation yesterday.

target: 결혼식은 이번 주 토요일 오후 두 시예요.
english: The wedding is this Saturday at 2 p.m.
The two finally got engaged last week.

target: 저는 친구의 결혼식에 꼭 갈 거예요.
english: I'll definitely go to my friend's wedding.
The bride was truly beautiful.
grammar: 아름답다 describes looks, so no -어하다: 신부가 아름다웠어요.

english: The groom seemed very nervous.
grammar: -(으)ㄴ 것 같다 for a past guess: 긴장한 것 같았어요.

english: You put the cash gift in an envelope to give.
There's a reception after the wedding.

target: 부모님께서 두 사람의 결혼을 축하해 주셨어요.
english: My parents congratulated the couple's marriage.
grammar: 께서 + -셨어요 keeps the honor on the elders as subject.

target: 저는 아직 결혼 생각이 전혀 없어요.
english: I have no thoughts of marriage at all yet.
The venue address is written on the invitation.

target: 우리는 작고 조용한 결혼식을 하고 싶어요.
english: We want a small, quiet wedding.
They decided to go to Jeju for the honeymoon.
Wedding preparation is much harder than expected.
Many guests congratulated the bride and groom.
My sister threw me the bouquet.
The two chose their wedding rings together.
The officiant's words were really moving.
grammar: 말씀 (malsseum) = honored 'words/speech' of an elder.

target: 결혼식에 뭘 입을지 아직 못 정했어요.
english: I haven't decided what to wear to the wedding.
I hope the two live happily for a long time.
grammar: -시길 바라요 = 'I hope (you, honored) ...': 행복하시길 바라요.

english: My friend made the invitations themselves and sent them.
The couple made their wedding photos into an album.
I sang a congratulatory song at my friend's wedding.
I sincerely bless the couple's future.
I really like K-pop.
grammar: 케이팝 (keipap) = K-pop, written as a loanword in hangul.

target: 다음 주에 좋아하는 가수의 콘서트에 가요.
english: I'm going to my favorite singer's concert next week.
grammar: 좋아하는 (joahaneun) = 'that (I) like' — verb + -는 modifies a noun.

target: 콘서트 표가 십 분 만에 다 매진됐어요.
english: The concert tickets all sold out in ten minutes.
grammar: 매진되다 (maejindoeda) = to sell out; -만에 = 'within/in just'.

target: 저는 응원봉을 흔들면서 노래를 따라 불렀어요.
english: I sang along waving my light stick.
grammar: -(으)면서 (-myeonseo) = 'while': 흔들면서 = while waving.

target: 그 아이돌 그룹은 전 세계에서 유명해요.
english: That idol group is famous all over the world.
grammar: 전 세계 (jeon segye) = the whole world.

target: 저는 이 노래 가사를 벌써 다 외웠어요.
english: I've already memorized all the lyrics to this song.
grammar: 가사 (gasa) = lyrics; 외우다 = to memorize.

english: The atmosphere at the concert was really electric.
grammar: 분위기 (bunwigi) = atmosphere/mood.

target: 팬들이 한 목소리로 가수 이름을 외쳤어요.
english: The fans shouted the singer's name in one voice.
grammar: 한 목소리로 (han moksoriro) = in one voice; 외치다 = to shout.

target: 저는 최애 멤버의 사진을 열심히 모아요.
english: I diligently collect photos of my favorite member.
grammar: 최애 (choeae) = one's very favorite — fandom slang from 最愛 (most-loved).

english: I bought the new album as soon as it came out.
grammar: -자마자 (-jamaja) = 'as soon as': 나오자마자 = as soon as it came out.

target: 그 가수는 춤과 노래를 둘 다 잘해요.
english: That singer is good at both dancing and singing.
grammar: 둘 다 (dul da) = 'both'; -와/과 = 'and': 춤과 노래.

english: They did as many as three encore songs.
grammar: -이나 (-ina) = 'as many as (surprisingly)': 세 곡이나.

english: The stage lighting was really dazzling.
grammar: 화려하다 (hwaryeohada) = to be splendid/dazzling.

target: 저는 그 가수의 공식 팬클럽에 가입했어요.
english: I joined that singer's official fan club.
grammar: 가입하다 (gaiphada) = to sign up / join.

target: 표를 못 구해서 콘서트를 생중계로 봤어요.
english: I couldn't get a ticket, so I watched the concert live-streamed.
grammar: 생중계 (saengjunggye) = a live broadcast/stream.

target: 그 그룹의 신곡이 음원 차트 일 위를 했어요.
english: That group's new song hit number one on the charts.
grammar: 신곡 (singok) = a new song; 일 위 = first place.

english: The feeling lingered long after the concert ended.
grammar: 여운이 남다 (yeouni namda) = the afterglow lingers.

target: 저는 데뷔 때부터 그들을 계속 응원했어요.
english: I've supported them ever since their debut.
grammar: -부터 (-buteo) = 'from/since': 데뷔 때부터 = since debut.

target: 표를 끝내 못 구해서 정말 아쉬웠어요.
english: I ended up not getting a ticket, so I was really disappointed.
A friend suggested we go to a signing event together.
grammar: -자고 하다 (-jago hada) = report a suggestion: 가자고 했어요.

target: 그 아이돌은 팬들을 정말 소중하게 생각해요.
english: That idol truly treasures the fans.
grammar: 소중하게 (sojunghage) = preciously; 생각하다 here = to regard.

target: 저는 그 콘서트 영상을 몇 번이나 다시 봤어요.
english: I rewatched that concert video several times.
grammar: 몇 번이나 (myeot beonina) = 'so many times', with emphatic -이나.

target: 무대 위의 그 가수가 정말 멋있었어요.
english: That singer on stage was really cool.
grammar: 위 (wi) = 'top/on'; -의 links nouns: 무대 위의 = on the stage.

english: I often sing K-pop at the karaoke room.
grammar: 노래방 (noraebang) = a karaoke room (song + room).

target: 열성 팬들이 가수를 위해 기부도 해요.
english: Devoted fans even donate for their singer.
grammar: -을/를 위해 (-eul wihae) = 'for (the sake of)': 가수를 위해.

target: 어제 친구랑 극장에 영화를 보러 갔어요.
english: Yesterday I went to the cinema with a friend to see a movie.
grammar: -(으)러 가다 (-reo gada) = 'go in order to': 보러 갔어요.

english: That movie's ending was really sad.
grammar: 결말 (gyeolmal) = ending; here 슬프다 describes the ending itself.

target: 저는 한국 드라마를 보면서 한국어를 배워요.
english: I learn Korean by watching Korean dramas.
grammar: -(으)면서 (-myeonseo) = 'while': 보면서 = while watching.

target: 이 드라마는 매주 금요일 밤에 방송해요.
english: This drama airs every Friday night.
grammar: 방송하다 (bangsonghada) = to broadcast/air.

english: The lead actor's acting was excellent.
grammar: 주인공 (juingong) = protagonist; 연기 = acting.

english: That movie was based on a true story.
grammar: -을 바탕으로 (-eul batangeuro) = 'based on': 실화를 바탕으로.

target: 다음 회가 너무 궁금해서 잠이 안 와요.
english: I'm so curious about the next episode I can't sleep.
grammar: 궁금하다 (gunggeumhada) = to be curious (I-feeling).

target: 저는 무서운 영화를 잘 못 봐요.
english: I can't really watch scary movies.
grammar: 무서운 (museoun) = 'scary' — 무섭다's noun-modifying form.

target: 이 드라마는 요즘 젊은 사람들한테 인기가 많아요.
english: This drama is very popular with young people these days.
grammar: 인기가 많다 (ingiga manta) = to be popular; -한테 = 'with/among'.

english: I bought popcorn at the cinema and ate it.
grammar: -아/어서 links order: 사서 먹었어요 = bought (it) and ate.

target: 그 배우는 이 작품으로 큰 상을 받았어요.
english: That actor won a big award for this work.
grammar: 작품 (jakpum) = a (creative) work; 상을 받다 = to win an award.

target: 저는 주말에 그 드라마를 밤새 몰아서 봤어요.
english: I binge-watched that drama all night on the weekend.
grammar: 몰아서 보다 (moraseo boda) = to binge-watch.

target: 저는 감동적인 영화를 보면 자주 울어요.
english: I often cry when I watch moving movies.
grammar: 감동적인 (gamdongjeogin) = moving/touching (noun-modifying).

target: 이 영화의 배경 음악이 정말 아름다워요.
english: This movie's background music is really beautiful.
grammar: 배경 음악 (baegyeong eumak) = background music/score.

target: 저는 그 드라마의 마지막 회를 놓쳤어요.
english: I missed the last episode of that drama.
grammar: 놓치다 (nochida) = to miss (catch); 마지막 회 = last episode.

english: My little brother likes action movies the best.
grammar: 남동생 (namdongsaeng) = younger brother (male sibling).

target: 영화가 시작하기 전에 광고가 너무 많아요.
english: There are too many ads before the movie starts.
grammar: -기 전에 (-gi jeone) = 'before': 시작하기 전에.

target: 저는 자막 없이 드라마를 이해하고 싶어요.
english: I want to understand dramas without subtitles.
grammar: 자막 (jamak) = subtitles; 없이 = 'without'.

target: 그 영화는 상영 시간이 두 시간이 넘어요.
english: That movie's running time is over two hours.
grammar: 넘다 (neomda) = to exceed: 두 시간이 넘어요.

english: I watch Netflix at home every weekend.
This scene is the highlight of this movie.
grammar: 장면 (jangmyeon) = scene; 명장면 = a famous/best scene.

english: The actor shared behind-the-scenes stories in an interview.
grammar: 촬영 (chwaryeong) = filming/shooting.

target: 그 인기 드라마는 소설을 원작으로 해요.
english: That popular drama is based on a novel.
grammar: -을 원작으로 하다 = 'be based on (an original work)'.

english: I teared up just from the trailer.
grammar: 예고편 (yegopyeon) = a trailer/preview; -고도 = 'even after'.

target: 친구가 이 영화를 꼭 보라고 추천했어요.
english: A friend recommended I definitely see this movie.

target: 저는 주말에 미술관에 전시를 보러 갔어요.
english: On the weekend I went to the art museum to see an exhibition.

target: 이 그림은 백 년도 더 전에 그린 거예요.
english: This painting was painted over a hundred years ago.
That exhibition's admission was free.

target: 저는 이 화가의 작품을 아주 좋아해요.
english: I really like this painter's works.

target: 미술관 안에서는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
english: You must not take photos inside the museum.
grammar: -(으)면 안 되다 = 'must not': 찍으면 안 돼요 = mustn't photograph.

target: 이 조각상은 실제로 보니까 훨씬 더 웅장해요.
english: This sculpture is far more grand in person.
That exhibition is only open until next month.

target: 해설사가 그림 하나하나를 자세히 설명해 줬어요.
english: The docent explained each painting in detail.

target: 저는 이 작품의 색이 정말 마음에 들어요.
english: I really like the colors of this work.
I bought a postcard as a souvenir at the museum.

target: 다행히 이 전시는 사진 촬영이 가능해요.
english: Luckily, photography is allowed at this exhibition.

target: 그 화가는 주로 조용한 시골 풍경을 그려요.
english: That painter mainly paints quiet rural landscapes.

target: 저는 추상화보다 풍경화를 훨씬 더 좋아해요.
english: I prefer landscape paintings much more than abstract ones.
Being the weekend, the exhibition hall was crowded.

target: 저는 이 작품 앞에서 한참 동안 서 있었어요.
english: I stood in front of this work for a long while.

target: 그 미술관은 매주 월요일에 문을 닫아요.
english: That museum is closed every Monday.

target: 아이들을 위한 체험 전시도 따로 있어요.
english: There's also a separate hands-on exhibition for children.

target: 저는 미술관에서 도록을 한 권 샀어요.
english: I bought a catalog at the museum.

target: 이 그림은 사진으로 볼 때보다 훨씬 커요.
english: This painting is much bigger than in photos.

target: 유명한 그림 앞에는 사람들 줄이 아주 길었어요.
english: The line in front of the famous painting was very long.

target: 그 특별 전시는 예약을 해야 볼 수 있어요.
english: You can only see that special exhibition with a reservation.
grammar: -아/어야 ... -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = 'can only ... if': 해야 볼 수 있어요.

target: 저는 아직 현대 미술을 잘 이해하지 못해요.
english: I still don't quite understand modern art.

target: 우리는 미술관 안 카페에서 잠깐 쉬었어요.
english: We rested for a bit at the cafe inside the museum.

target: 이 젊은 작가는 아주 어린 나이에 유명해졌어요.
english: This young artist became famous at a very young age.

target: 전시를 다 보고 나니까 새 영감이 떠올랐어요.
english: After seeing the whole exhibition, new inspiration came to me.

target: 저는 한 달에 책을 두 권씩 읽어요.
english: I read two books a month.

target: 이 소설은 끝까지 손에서 놓을 수가 없었어요.
english: I couldn't put this novel down until the end.
What book are you reading these days?

target: 저는 이 작가의 담담한 문체가 정말 좋아요.
english: I really like this author's calm writing style.

target: 저는 자기 전에 항상 책을 조금 읽어요.
english: I always read a bit before I sleep.

target: 그 책은 요즘 베스트셀러라서 다 팔렸어요.
english: That book is a current bestseller, so it's all sold out.

target: 저는 어제 도서관에서 책을 세 권 빌렸어요.
english: I borrowed three books from the library yesterday.

target: 저는 이 시집을 친구에게 생일 선물로 줬어요.
english: I gave this poetry book to a friend as a birthday gift.
I much prefer paper books to e-books.

target: 이 책의 마지막 문장이 오래 기억에 남아요.
english: The last sentence of this book stays with me.

target: 저는 독서 모임에서 매달 책을 한 권씩 읽어요.
english: At my book club we read one book each month.

target: 그 소설은 인기가 많아서 영화로도 만들어졌어요.
english: That novel was so popular it was even made into a movie.

target: 저는 어려운 책은 보통 두 번씩 읽어요.
english: I usually read difficult books twice.

target: 이 책을 읽고 나서 생각이 많이 바뀌었어요.
english: After reading this book, my thinking changed a lot.

target: 저는 여러 장르 중에서 추리 소설을 제일 좋아해요.
english: Of all genres, I like mystery novels the best.

target: 저는 주말에 서점에서 신간을 한참 구경했어요.
english: On the weekend I browsed new releases at the bookstore for a while.

target: 저는 작가의 사인이 담긴 책을 한 권 샀어요.
english: I bought a book with the author's autograph.

target: 이 외국 소설은 번역이 아주 잘 됐어요.
english: This foreign novel was translated very well.

target: 저는 책을 읽으면서 중요한 곳에 밑줄을 그어요.
english: I underline important parts while reading.

target: 그 에세이는 짧지만 여운이 아주 길어요.
english: That essay is short but its resonance is very long.

target: 저는 아이에게 매일 밤 동화책을 읽어 줘요.
english: I read a fairy tale to my child every night.
The illustrations in this picture book are really pretty.

target: 저는 다 읽은 책을 친구에게 자주 빌려줘요.
english: I often lend books I've finished to friends.

target: 저는 그 작가의 새 책을 손꼽아 기다려요.
english: I'm eagerly awaiting that author's new book.

target: 좋은 책 한 권이 사람의 마음을 바꿔요.
english: One good book changes a person's heart.

target: 저는 어제 처음으로 판소리 공연을 봤어요.
english: Yesterday I saw a pansori performance for the first time.

target: 판소리는 한 사람이 북장단에 맞춰 노래해요.
english: In pansori, one person sings to a drum beat.

target: 사물놀이는 네 가지 전통 악기로 연주해요.
english: Samulnori is played with four traditional instruments.
The kkwaenggwari sound was really loud and powerful.

target: 저는 전통 음악을 제대로 배워 보고 싶어요.
english: I want to properly try learning traditional music.
The audience enthusiastically added chuimsae calls.

target: 사물놀이 장단이 뒤로 갈수록 점점 빨라졌어요.
english: The samulnori rhythm got faster and faster toward the end.
My grandmother really loves pansori.
grammar: Elder subject → 좋아하세요 (joahaseyo), the honorific present.

target: 그 소리꾼의 목소리가 정말 힘이 있었어요.
english: That singer's voice was really powerful.

target: 저는 장구를 조금 칠 줄 알아요.
english: I can play the janggu a little.

target: 전통 공연은 외국인 관광객들에게도 인기가 많아요.
english: Traditional performances are popular with foreign tourists too.

target: 저는 탈춤을 보면서 저도 모르게 크게 웃었어요.
english: I laughed out loud without realizing while watching the mask dance.
Every movement of the fan dance is really elegant.

target: 명절에는 마을에서 사물놀이 공연을 자주 해요.
english: During the holidays the village often holds samulnori shows.

target: 저는 국악 공연을 미리 온라인으로 예매했어요.
english: I booked the Korean-music performance online in advance.

target: 판소리 한 마당은 보통 몇 시간이나 걸려요.
english: One full pansori piece usually takes several hours.

target: 판소리에서 북 치는 사람을 고수라고 불러요.
english: In pansori, the drummer is called a gosu.

target: 전통 악기 소리가 신기하게 마음을 편하게 해 줘요.
english: The sound of traditional instruments strangely calms the heart.

target: 저는 어릴 때 몇 년 동안 가야금을 배웠어요.
english: I learned gayageum for a few years as a child.

target: 공연이 끝나자 관객들이 다 같이 박수를 쳤어요.
english: When the performance ended, the whole audience clapped.
Samulnori originally started from rural farmers' music.

target: 그 공연은 전통과 현대를 멋지게 함께 보여 줬어요.
english: That show wonderfully brought together tradition and modernity.

target: 저는 판소리 사설을 이해하기가 조금 어려웠어요.
english: I found the pansori narration a bit hard to understand.

target: 요즘 젊은 예술가들이 국악을 새롭게 바꿔요.
english: These days young artists are reinventing Korean music.

target: 전통 예술을 지키는 일은 정말 소중해요.
english: Preserving traditional art is truly precious.
I'm going on an overseas trip next month.
grammar: 해외 (haeoe) = overseas: 해외여행 = trip abroad, 국내 여행 = domestic trip.

english: I got my passport ready in advance.
I arrived at the airport three hours early.
grammar: Hours of duration use native numbers: 세 시간 (se sigan) = three hours.

english: Where do I check in?
Please show your boarding pass here.
grammar: 보여 주세요 (boyeo juseyo) = please show me — 보이다 + 주다.

english: My luggage is heavier than I thought.
grammar: 무겁다 flips ㅂ to 우: 무거워요 (mugeowoyo) = is heavy.

english: How many kilos of baggage are allowed?
A window seat, please.
grammar: (으)로 marks the choice: 창가 자리로 (changga jariro) = as a window seat.

english: An aisle seat is more comfortable.
I'm not sure where the gate is.
grammar: -ㄴ지 embeds a question: 어디인지 (eodi-inji) = where it is.

english: The flight was delayed two hours.
I got through departure screening quickly.
I bought cosmetics at the duty-free shop.
Please fasten your seatbelt.

target: 이 짐은 기내에 들고 탈 거예요.
english: I'll carry this bag on board.
grammar: 들고 타다 = carry on: 들고 탈 거예요 = will carry it aboard.

english: The layover time is plenty.
I transferred to the next flight.
grammar: 갈아타다 = to transfer: 갈아탔어요 (garatasseoyo) = changed transport.

english: I'm going to Paris via a connection.
The flight took twelve hours.
The in-flight meal was tastier than expected.
I stood in line a long time at immigration.
What is the purpose of your visit?
I came to do some sightseeing.
grammar: -러 marks purpose of going: 관광하러 (gwangwanghareo) = in order to sightsee.

english: How long will you stay?
I'll be here about a week.
grammar: 정도 (jeongdo) = about, roughly: 일주일 정도 = about a week.

english: I'll be staying at a hotel.
Please scan your fingerprint here.
I filled out the arrival card in advance.
I opened my bag at customs.
I have nothing to declare.
Where is baggage claim?
grammar: -는 곳 = the place where: 짐을 찾는 곳 (channeun got) = baggage claim.

english: My baggage hasn't come out yet.
grammar: 아직 안 = not yet: 아직 안 나왔어요 (ajik an nawasseoyo).

english: I bought a SIM card at the airport.
Where do I exchange money?
I took the airport bus into the city.
I applied for a visa.
I came on a tourist visa.
I need a student visa.
You can go to Korea visa-free.
grammar: 무비자 (mubija) = visa-free: 무- means "without".

english: I'd like to extend my visa.
I submitted documents to the embassy.
The visa comes out next week.
My passport expires soon.
The visa is valid for three months.
grammar: Months of duration use Sino numbers: 삼 개월 (sam gaewol) = 3 months.

english: I searched for the consulate location.
I'm missing one document.
I took new visa photos.
I'll go study a language abroad next year.
grammar: 어학연수 (eohangnyeonsu — ㄴ inserted, ㄱ→ㅇ) = studying a language abroad.

english: I came to Seoul to study.
grammar: 유학 (yuhak) = studying abroad: 유학을 왔어요 = came to study.

english: I enrolled at a language school.
I'll study for one semester.
grammar: 동안 = for a duration: 한 학기 동안 = for one semester.

english: The tuition is a bit expensive.
I took the placement test.
I got into the intermediate class.
grammar: 중급 (junggeup) = intermediate level; 초급 = beginner, 고급 = advanced.

english: I live in a dormitory.
My homestay family is really kind.
My host mother cooks well.
grammar: Elders take -세요: 잘하세요 (jalhaseyo) shows respect.

english: I came as an exchange student.
Class starts at nine in the morning.
grammar: Clock hours use native numbers: 아홉 시 (ahop si) = nine oclock.

english: There's a lot of homework every day.
The speaking test is the hardest.
I made a lot of Korean friends.
I study at the library after class.
grammar: 후에 = after: 수업 후에 (sueop hue) = after class.

english: My pronunciation has improved a lot.
The teacher speaks slowly.
grammar: 말씀하시다 = to speak (honorific): 말씀하세요 for a teacher.

english: I want to get a scholarship.
I'll travel around during the break.
I'm preparing for the Korean proficiency test.
I'm gradually getting used to local life.
grammar: 익숙해지다 = to get used to: 익숙해져요 (iksukaejyeoyo).

english: I received a certificate of completion.
I'll register for next semester too.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise: 등록할게요 (deungnokalgeyo) = I will register.

english: I get along well with my roommate.
At first I had culture shock.
grammar: 문화충격 (munhwachunggyeok) = culture shock: 충격을 받다 = be shocked.

english: There is a tipping culture here.
The culture is very different from Korea's.
grammar: 와/과 다르다 = different from: 한국하고 달라요 (dallayo).

english: Table manners differ from ours.
The way people greet is different.
grammar: -는 방법 = the way of: 인사하는 방법 = way of greeting.

english: I don't know this country's customs well.
At first everything felt unfamiliar.
Now I've gotten quite used to it.
People here are really friendly.
I was surprised the shops close early.
grammar: -아서 gives a cause: 닫아서 (dadaseo) = because it closes.

english: The local food suits my taste well.
grammar: 입에 맞다 = to suit ones taste: 입에 맞아요 (ibe majayo).

english: Sometimes I miss spicy food.
grammar: 그립다 flips ㅂ to 우: 그리워요 (geuriwoyo) = I miss it.

english: The weather is the opposite of Korea's.
Life abroad is harder than I thought.
I felt frustrated because I couldn't communicate.
grammar: 말이 통하다 = to communicate: 안 통해서 = because it doesnt get through.

english: I barely explained with gestures.
A local friend helped me a lot.
I got lost because I didn't know how to take the bus.

target: 시차 때문에 밤에 잠이 안 와요.
english: I can't sleep at night because of jet lag.
grammar: 시차 (sicha) = time difference/jet lag: 시차 때문에 = because of jet lag.

english: Prices are higher than in Korea.
This city feels comfortable to me now.
I met friends from various countries.
My homesickness is bad these days.
grammar: 향수병 (hyangsubyeong) = homesickness (lit. nostalgia illness).

english: I really miss my family.
grammar: 보고 싶다 = to miss (a person): 보고 싶어요 (bogo sipeoyo).

english: I video-call my parents every day.
My mom misses me a lot.
grammar: 3rd-person feelings take -어하다: 그리워하세요 (geuriwohaseyo) = (she) misses.

english: My younger sibling wonders how I am.
grammar: Others' curiosity uses -어하다: 궁금해해요 (gunggeumhaehaeyo).

english: I keep thinking of Korean food.
When I miss home, I look at photos.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 때 = when: 그리울 때 (geuriul ttae) = when I miss it.

english: I feel lonely when I'm alone at night.
My friends worry about me.
Hearing my parents' voices gives me strength.
grammar: 들으면: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular — 들으면 (deureumyeon) = if/when I hear.

english: I put a family photo on my desk.
I make sure to watch Korean news every day.
grammar: 챙겨 보다 = to make a point of watching: 챙겨 봐요.

english: I miss my family especially on holidays.
grammar: 명절 (myeongjeol) = traditional holiday.

english: I want to eat the kimchi stew my mom makes.
grammar: -고 싶다 = to want to: 먹고 싶어요 (meokgo sipeoyo).

english: A friend sent me a package.
As time passed it got a little better.
grammar: -(으)니까 = as/since: 지나니까 (jinanikka) = as time passes.

english: I bought ramen at the Korean grocery store.
My family says they'll come visit soon.
grammar: -ㄴ대요 relays what was said: 온대요 (ondaeyo) = (they) say they'll come.

english: It took time to adjust.
grammar: -는 데 = for the task of: 적응하는 데 (jeogeunghaneun de) = to adjust.

english: Now this place feels like a second home.

target: 방학에 한국에 갈 생각을 하면 설레요.
english: I get excited thinking about going to Korea on break.
I write letters to my parents often.
grammar: 께 is the honorific 에게: 부모님께 (bumonimkke) = to (my) parents.

english: Whenever things are hard I think of my family.
grammar: -ㄹ 때마다 = every time: 힘들 때마다 (himdeul ttaemada).

english: They weighed my bag when I checked it in.

target: 비상구 좌석은 다리를 뻗을 수 있어요.
english: Emergency-exit seats let you stretch your legs.
I slept the whole flight.
I got an entry stamp in my passport.
I rented a car at the airport.
A local SIM is much cheaper.
I was very nervous since it was my first trip abroad.
grammar: -이라서 = because it is: 첫 여행이라서 (yeohaeng-iraseo).

english: I rested briefly in the airport lounge.
In my opinion, that is right.
grammar: 제 생각에는 (je saenggageneun) = in my opinion — a soft opinion opener.

english: I don't necessarily think so.
grammar: -지 않다 negates: 생각하지 않아요 (saenggakaji anayo) = I dont think so.

english: I think this plan is good.
grammar: ~다고 생각해요 = I think that ~: 좋다고 생각해요 (jotago saenggakaeyo).

english: I think that is correct.
grammar: ~것 같아요 softens a claim: 맞는 것 같아요 (manneun geot gatayo) = seems right.

english: My opinion is a bit different from that.
grammar: 의견 (uigyeon) = opinion: 제 의견은 = my opinion is.

english: Personally, I'm against it.
Honestly, I'm not sure.
grammar: 솔직히 말하면 (soljiki malhamyeon — 직히 sounds like 지키) = to be honest.

english: The way I see it, there is a problem.
That opinion makes sense.
grammar: 일리가 있다 = to have a point: 일리가 있어요 (illiga isseoyo).

english: This differs from person to person.
I think the same.
I'm not certain, but it's probably so.
grammar: -지는 않지만 = not quite, but: 확실하지는 않지만.

english: I'll share my honest opinion.
I'll give it some thought.
grammar: -아/어 볼게요 = I will try: 생각해 볼게요 (saenggakae bolgeyo).

english: I admit that point too.
From my position, it doesn't make sense.
grammar: 입장 (ipjang) = position/stance: 제 입장에서는 = from my standpoint.

target: 이 문제는 좀 더 고민해야 해요.
english: We need to think this over more.
grammar: -아야 하다 = must: 고민해야 해요 (gominhaeya haeyo) = must ponder.

english: Many people feel that way.
I have my own reasons.
That depends on the situation.
grammar: -에 따라 = depending on: 상황에 따라 (sanghwange ttara).

english: I agree with the part you mentioned.
My conclusion is this.
I support that opinion.
grammar: 찬성하다 = to be in favor: 찬성해요 (chanseonghaeyo) = I agree/support.

english: I'm against that plan.
grammar: 반대하다 = to oppose: 반대해요 (bandaehaeyo) = I object.

english: I completely agree with that.
grammar: 동의하다 = to agree: 완전히 동의해요 (wanjeonhi dongihaeyo).

english: I think so too.
I'd like to object to that point.
It's right to some degree.
grammar: 어느 정도 (eoneu jeongdo) = to some extent.

english: I don't think that's quite right.
grammar: 아닌 것 같아요 = seems not so — a polite disagreement.

english: There are more people in favor.
I want to hear the reasons against.
It's not that I oppose that opinion.
grammar: -는 건 아니에요 = its not that: softens the stance.

english: I only partly agree.
I respect that view too.
We can think differently from each other.
grammar: 서로 (seoro) = each other; -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = can.

english: I'm a bit skeptical of that opinion.
Opinions split evenly for and against.
grammar: 찬반 (chanban) = pro and con: 찬반으로 갈리다 = split into for/against.

english: It'd be best to follow the majority view.

target: 근거를 들면 이렇게 설명할 수 있어요.
english: To give grounds, I can explain it this way.
grammar: 근거를 들다 = to cite grounds: 근거를 들면 (geungeoreul deulmyeon).

english: For example, there are cases like this.
grammar: 예를 들면 (yereul deulmyeon) = for example.

english: It's because there isn't enough time.
grammar: 왜냐하면 ~기 때문에 = because: 부족하기 때문이에요.

english: First, it costs too much.
grammar: 첫째 (cheotjjae) = firstly: 첫째로 = first of all.

english: Second, it also takes a long time.
According to statistics, that isn't so.
grammar: -에 따르면 = according to: 통계에 따르면 (tonggye-e ttareumyeon).

english: Research results show that.
It's clear when you look at the data.
A concrete example is needed.
I'm speaking based on my experience.
grammar: -을 근거로 = based on: 경험을 근거로 (gyeongheomeul geungeoro).

english: There are broadly two reasons.
That claim lacks evidence.
Experts say the same thing too.
We should check the facts first.
You shouldn't speak without grounds.
grammar: -면 안 되다 = must not: 말하면 안 돼요 (malhamyeon an dwaeyo).

english: I think environmental issues are the most important.
We should recycle more diligently.
We should reduce plastic use.
Technology has changed our lives.
I worry AI might cut jobs.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ까 봐 = worried that: 줄일까 봐 (juril-kka bwa).

english: It's hard to live without a smartphone.
grammar: 없이는 = without: 스마트폰 없이는 (seumateupon eopsineun).

english: Social media has pros and cons.

target: 소셜미디어를 너무 많이 하면 안 좋아요.
english: It's not good to overuse social media.
I think the education system should change.
Exam-centered education is a problem.
grammar: 위주 (wiju) = -centered: 시험 위주 = exam-focused.

english: Working from home is more efficient.
grammar: 재택근무 (jaetaekgeunmu) = remote work; 효율적 = efficient.

english: Remote work has downsides too.
I think city life is more convenient.
The countryside is nicer to live in than the city.
grammar: 살기 좋다 = good to live in: 살기 좋아요 (salgi joayo).

english: It's good to use public transport.
Work-life balance is really important.
grammar: 워라밸 (worabael) = work-life balance — a clipped loanword.

english: The younger generation thinks differently.
Online classes have many advantages too.
Health is more important than money.
Exercise helps relieve stress.
Reading develops thinking skills.
Learning a foreign language broadens your view.
Cutting disposables is good for the environment.
Electric cars will grow more common in the future.

target: 가짜 뉴스가 사회에 나쁜 영향을 줘요.
english: Fake news has a bad influence on society.
grammar: 영향을 주다 = to influence: 영향을 줘요 (yeonghyangeul jwoyo).

english: You shouldn't just believe information as is.
Don't trust ads too much.
grammar: -지 마세요 = please dont: 믿지 마세요 (mitji maseyo).

english: I think low birth rates are a serious problem.
I'm worried because housing is too expensive.
Volunteering helps society.
But we should look at the other side too.
grammar: 하지만 (hajiman) = but, however — starts a contrast.

english: On the other hand, there are these problems too.
grammar: 반면에 (banmyeone) = on the other hand.

english: Still, I tend to be in favor.
grammar: -는 편이다 = tend to: 찬성하는 편이에요 (chanseonghaneun pyeonieyo).

english: Of course there are downsides, but it's fine.
In a way, both are right.
grammar: 어떻게 보면 (eotteoke bomyeon) = in a sense.

english: You can't necessarily say that's so.
grammar: 꼭 ~ 것은 아니다 = not necessarily: 꼭 그렇다고 볼 수 없어요.

english: Neither side is perfect.
On reflection, I was wrong.
grammar: -아 보니 = upon doing: 생각해 보니 (saenggakae boni) = now that I think.

english: I hadn't thought of that point.
Now that I hear it, it makes sense.
grammar: -고 보니 = after doing: 듣고 보니 (deutgo boni).

english: I opposed it at first, but now I agree.
I hope we each give a little.
In conclusion, I support this proposal.
grammar: 결론적으로 (gyeolloncheogeuro) = in conclusion.

english: To summarize, two things are key.
grammar: 요약하면 (yoyakamyeon) = to summarize; 핵심 = the crux.

english: In other words, we need more time.
grammar: 다시 말하면 (dasi malhamyeon) = in other words.

english: To put it in order, it comes to this.
In the end the choice is up to each person.

target: 이 정도면 충분히 설명한 것 같아요.
english: I think that explains it well enough.
grammar: 이 정도면 = at this level: 이 정도면 충분해요 = this much is enough.

english: Lastly, I'll add just one thing.
grammar: 끝으로 (kkeuteuro) = lastly; 덧붙이다 = to add on.

english: I think it was a good discussion.
Thanks, everyone, for sharing your opinions.
Let's talk more deeply next time.
That topic is very controversial.
People's opinions are sharply divided.
I want to stay neutral.
Facts matter more than emotions.
You should hear the other person out fully.
grammar: 상대방 (sangdaebang) = the other party; 끝까지 = to the end.

english: We should lend an ear to opposing views too.
grammar: 귀를 기울이다 = to lend an ear: 귀를 기울여요.

english: In a debate you must be polite.
Please don't misunderstand me.
A grounded argument is persuasive.
We need diverse perspectives.
There is no single right answer to this.
We should try to understand each other.
grammar: -려고 = in order to: 이해하려고 노력해요 = try to understand.

english: We shouldn't make the decision hastily.
I back that opinion.
grammar: 지지하다 = to support/back: 지지해요 (jijihaeyo).

target: 이 논의는 시간이 좀 걸릴 것 같아요.
english: This discussion will probably take a while.
Each person has their own stance.
grammar: 각자 (gakja) = each; 자기 (jagi) = ones own.

english: We must find a better direction.
Cooperation yields better results.
We need alternatives more than criticism.
Good questions make good discussions.
grammar: 만들다 keeps ㄹ before -어: 만들어요 (mandeureoyo) = makes.

target: 본 열차는 잠시 후 종착역인 부산역에 도착하겠습니다. 두고 내리시는 물건이 없도록 다시 한번 확인하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: This train will shortly arrive at its final stop, Busan Station. Please check once more that you have not left any belongings behind.
grammar: -겠습니다 states a formal announced future: 도착하겠습니다 (dochakhagetseumnida = will arrive).

target: 귀하께서 제출하신 지원 서류를 검토한 결과, 면접 대상자로 선정되셨음을 알려 드립니다.
english: Having reviewed the application documents you submitted, we are pleased to inform you that you have been selected for an interview.
grammar: Formal notice ending -음을 알려 드립니다 (…eumeul allyeo deurimnida = we hereby inform you that…).

target: 지금부터 신랑 신부의 입장이 있겠습니다. 하객 여러분께서는 큰 박수로 맞아 주시기 바랍니다.
english: The bride and groom will now enter. Guests, please welcome them with a warm round of applause.
grammar: -이/가 있겠습니다 announces an event formally: 입장이 있겠습니다 (ipjang-i itgetseumnida = there will be an entrance).

target: 승객 여러분의 안전을 위하여 비행기가 완전히 멈춘 후 자리에서 일어나 주시기 바랍니다.
english: For your safety, please remain seated until the aircraft has come to a complete stop.

target: 이번 분기 실적 부진의 책임을 통감하며, 이 자리를 빌려 깊이 사죄드립니다.
english: I keenly feel my responsibility for this quarter's poor performance, and I take this opportunity to offer my sincere apology.

target: 삼가 고인의 명복을 빌며, 유가족 여러분께 깊은 위로의 말씀을 전합니다.
english: I humbly pray for the repose of the deceased and offer my deepest condolences to the bereaved family.
grammar: 삼가 (samga = respectfully) opens formal condolences: 삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다 (= I humbly pray for the deceased).

target: 본 미술관은 오후 6시에 폐관하오니 관람에 참고하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: This museum closes at 6 p.m.; please bear this in mind when planning your visit.
grammar: -하오니 is a formal written 'since': 폐관하오니 (pyegwanhaoni = since it closes).

target: 계약 조건에 대한 상호 합의가 이루어지는 대로 정식 계약서를 발송해 드리겠습니다.
english: As soon as mutual agreement on the contract terms is reached, we will dispatch the formal contract.

target: 정부는 물가 안정을 위하여 가능한 모든 조치를 강구하고 있습니다.
english: The government is devising every possible measure to stabilize prices.

target: 바쁘신 와중에도 저희 아버님의 팔순 잔치에 참석해 주셔서 진심으로 감사드립니다.
english: Thank you sincerely for attending my father's 80th birthday celebration despite your busy schedule.

target: 다음 역은 이 열차의 종착역이므로, 모든 승객께서는 잊으신 물건이 없는지 살피신 후 하차하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: The next station is this train's final stop, so all passengers are asked to check for any forgotten belongings before disembarking.

target: 오랜 숙고 끝에, 저는 회사를 떠나기로 결심하였음을 알려 드립니다.
english: After long deliberation, I wish to inform you that I have decided to leave the company.
grammar: -하였음을 is the formal past nominalizer: 결심하였음을 (gyeolsimhayeosseumeul = that I decided).

target: 이번 전시는 국내 최초로 공개되는 작품들로 구성되어 있습니다.
english: This exhibition consists of works being unveiled domestically for the first time.

target: 부모님의 크신 은혜에 보답하고자 늘 최선을 다하겠습니다.
english: I will always do my utmost to repay my parents' great kindness.
grammar: -고자 = formal 'in order to': 보답하고자 (bodaphagoja = in order to repay).

target: 호텔 이용에 불편함이 없으시도록 저희 직원이 최선을 다해 모시겠습니다.
english: Our staff will do their utmost to serve you so that your stay is free of any inconvenience.

target: 첨부해 드린 자료를 검토하신 후, 늦어도 금주 내로 회신하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: After reviewing the attached materials, please reply no later than the end of this week.
grammar: 회신하다 (hoesinhada = to reply) is formal business vocabulary for 답장하다 (dapjanghada).

target: 본 방송은 청취자 여러분의 후원으로 제작되었음을 밝힙니다.
english: We wish to state that this program was produced with the support of our listeners.

target: 할머니께서 평소에 늘 하시던 말씀이 요즘 들어 더욱 마음에 사무칩니다.
english: The words my grandmother always used to say resonate all the more deeply in my heart these days.

target: 귀하의 노고에 깊이 감사드리며, 앞으로도 변함없는 협조를 부탁드립니다.
english: We deeply appreciate your hard work and ask for your continued cooperation.
grammar: 노고 (nogo = hard work/toil) is a formal 한자어 for acknowledging others' effort.

target: 기상 악화로 인하여 예정된 항공편이 지연되고 있음을 안내해 드립니다.
english: We wish to announce that the scheduled flight is delayed due to inclement weather.
grammar: -(으)로 인하여 = formal 'due to': 악화로 인하여 (akhwaro inhayeo = due to worsening).

target: 인간의 존엄성은 그 어떤 이유로도 훼손되어서는 안 됩니다.
english: Human dignity must not be violated for any reason whatsoever.

target: 신입 사원 여러분을 우리 회사의 일원으로 맞이하게 되어 매우 뜻깊게 생각합니다.
english: We find it deeply meaningful to welcome you, our new employees, as members of our company.

target: 형님 내외분께서 이렇게 먼 길을 마다하지 않고 찾아 주시니 그저 감사할 따름입니다.
english: I am simply grateful that my elder brother and his wife did not begrudge the long journey to visit us.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ 따름입니다 = formal 'simply/nothing but': 감사할 따름입니다 (gamsahal ttarumimnida = simply grateful).

target: 관람객 여러분의 원활한 이동을 위하여 지정된 통로를 이용하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: For the smooth movement of all visitors, please use the designated pathways.

target: 오늘 이 자리에 서게 된 것을 무한한 영광으로 생각합니다.
english: I consider it an infinite honor to stand here today.

target: 회의 안건은 사전에 배포된 자료를 참고하시되, 추가 의견은 서면으로 제출해 주십시오.
english: Please refer to the materials distributed in advance for the agenda, and submit any additional opinions in writing.
grammar: -십시오 is the 하십시오체 formal command: 제출해 주십시오 (jechulhae jusipsio = please submit).

target: 자식 된 도리로서 부모님을 봉양하는 것은 마땅한 일이라 생각합니다.
english: As a child, I believe it is only right to care for one's parents.

target: 본 유람선은 안전을 위하여 정원을 초과하여 탑승하실 수 없음을 알려 드립니다.
english: For safety reasons, this cruise boat may not be boarded beyond its capacity.

target: 자연은 우리가 후손에게 잠시 빌려 쓰는 것에 지나지 않습니다.
english: Nature is nothing more than something we borrow briefly from our descendants.
grammar: -에 지나지 않다 = formal 'nothing more than': 것에 지나지 않습니다 (…e jinaji anseumnida = is nothing but).

target: 그동안 보내 주신 성원과 격려에 힘입어 무사히 프로젝트를 완수할 수 있었습니다.
english: Thanks to the support and encouragement you have given, we were able to complete the project without incident.

target: 어머님의 손맛이 담긴 이 음식을 이제는 맛볼 수 없다는 것이 못내 아쉽습니다.
english: It is deeply regrettable that I can no longer taste the food made with my mother's touch.

target: 본 위원회는 국민의 목소리에 귀 기울일 것을 엄숙히 약속드립니다.
english: This committee solemnly promises to listen to the voice of the people.
grammar: 엄숙히 (eomsukhi = solemnly) is a formal adverb for pledges: 엄숙히 약속드립니다 (= solemnly promise).

target: 여권과 탑승권을 미리 준비하시어 수속이 지연되지 않도록 협조하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: Please have your passport and boarding pass ready in advance so that check-in is not delayed.
grammar: -시어 is a formal honorific connective 'and/so': 준비하시어 (junbihasieo = please prepare and…).

target: 부득이한 사정으로 회의 일정을 다음 주로 연기하게 되었음을 양해 바랍니다.
english: Due to unavoidable circumstances, the meeting has been postponed to next week; your understanding is appreciated.
grammar: 부득이한 (budeugihan = unavoidable) is formal vocabulary for explaining changes.

target: 본 관광 안내소에서는 외국인 방문객을 위한 다국어 통역 서비스를 제공하고 있습니다.
english: This tourist information center provides multilingual interpretation services for foreign visitors.

target: 조부님께서 남기신 유언을 저희 형제는 한시도 잊은 적이 없습니다.
english: We brothers have never for a moment forgotten the will our grandfather left behind.

target: 당사의 제품에 깊은 관심을 보여 주신 데 대하여 진심으로 감사의 말씀을 드립니다.
english: We sincerely thank you for the deep interest you have shown in our products.

target: 매표소는 오전 9시에 개장하오니 그 시간에 맞추어 방문하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: The ticket office opens at 9 a.m., so please plan your visit accordingly.

target: 장남으로서 집안의 대소사를 챙기는 일이 어느덧 저의 몫이 되었습니다.
english: As the eldest son, taking care of the family's affairs, big and small, has become my duty before I knew it.

target: 며느리로서 시부모님을 정성껏 모시는 것은 저에게 크나큰 기쁨입니다.
english: As a daughter-in-law, serving my parents-in-law with devotion is a great joy to me.

target: 향후 사업 방향에 대해 임직원 여러분의 기탄없는 의견을 구하고자 합니다.
english: We wish to seek your candid opinions on the company's future direction.
grammar: 기탄없는 (gitaneomneun = frank/candid) is a formal expression inviting open opinion.

target: 현재 도로 사정으로 인하여 목적지까지 다소 지연될 수 있음을 미리 안내해 드립니다.
english: Due to current road conditions, we inform you in advance that there may be some delay in reaching the destination.

target: 오랜 세월 이어져 온 전통이 한순간에 사라지는 것은 참으로 안타까운 일입니다.
english: It is truly regrettable that a tradition carried on for ages should vanish in an instant.

target: 채용 절차와 관련하여 궁금하신 사항은 인사팀으로 문의하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: For any questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact the HR team.

target: 부모님 슬하에서 자란 그 시절이 제 인생에서 가장 행복한 때였습니다.
english: The days I spent growing up under my parents' care were the happiest time of my life.

target: 본 연구 결과는 향후 정책 수립에 중요한 근거로 활용될 것입니다.
english: The findings of this study will serve as important grounds for future policymaking.

target: 객실 내 흡연은 엄격히 금지되어 있으며, 이를 위반하실 경우 별도의 벌금이 부과됩니다.
english: Smoking in the guest rooms is strictly prohibited, and violations will incur a separate fine.

target: 이번 인사 발령에 따라 다음 달부터 새로운 부서에서 근무하게 되었습니다.
english: In accordance with this personnel order, I will be working in a new department starting next month.

target: 위기의 순간일수록 우리는 더욱 냉철하게 판단하여야 합니다.
english: The more critical the moment, the more coolly we must judge.
grammar: -여야 하다 is formal written 'must': 판단하여야 합니다 (pandanhayeoya hamnida = must judge).

target: 손주들의 웃음소리가 온 집안에 가득할 때 비로소 사는 보람을 느낍니다.
english: Only when the grandchildren's laughter fills the whole house do I truly feel that life is worthwhile.

target: 안내 말씀 드리겠습니다. 잠시 후 우리 비행기는 인천국제공항에 착륙할 예정입니다.
english: May I have your attention. Shortly, our aircraft will be landing at Incheon International Airport.
grammar: 안내 말씀 드리겠습니다 (annae malsseum deurigetseumnida) is the set formal opener for announcements.

target: 상기 내용에 이의가 없으실 경우, 하단에 서명하여 주시기 바랍니다.
english: If you have no objection to the above, please sign at the bottom.
grammar: 상기 (sanggi = the above-stated) is formal document vocabulary referring to prior text.

target: 배움에는 나이가 없다는 말처럼, 저는 늦게나마 다시 공부를 시작하였습니다.
english: As the saying goes that learning has no age, I have begun studying again, late though it may be.

target: 장인어른의 환갑을 맞이하여 온 가족이 오랜만에 한자리에 모였습니다.
english: On the occasion of my father-in-law's 60th birthday, the whole family gathered together for the first time in a long while.

target: 예산 삭감이 불가피한 상황이오나, 핵심 사업만큼은 반드시 지켜 나가겠습니다.
english: Although budget cuts are unavoidable, we will surely protect the core projects at the very least.
grammar: -(이)오나 = formal written 'although': 상황이오나 (sanghwang-iona = though it is the situation).

target: 표현의 자유는 민주주의 사회의 근간을 이루는 소중한 가치입니다.
english: Freedom of expression is a precious value that forms the foundation of a democratic society.

target: 짐을 분실하셨을 경우, 3층에 위치한 유실물 센터로 문의하여 주십시오.
english: Should you lose your luggage, please inquire at the lost-and-found center located on the third floor.

target: 자녀 교육에 있어 부모의 솔선수범만큼 값진 가르침은 없다고 봅니다.
english: When it comes to raising children, I believe there is no lesson more valuable than a parent setting an example.

target: 오늘 회의에서 결정된 사항은 추후 공문을 통해 정식으로 통보될 예정입니다.
